question_text: What is meant by ionic product of water? Give its value at 25 °C.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Chemical Equilibrium, Acids and Bases · 2 marks

steps.label: The definition
lines: Water ionises to a very small extent:
The ionic product of water Kw is the product
of the concentrations of H⁺ (as H₃O⁺) and
OH⁻ ions in pure water or in any aqueous
steps.why: Kw is a product of two ion concentrations, so the definition needs both the ionisation equation and the expression [H⁺][OH⁻] — the words alone do not show what is multiplied.
common_mistakes: Writing Kw = [H⁺] + [OH⁻]. Kw is a product, not a sum.
Restricting the definition to pure water only. The product [H⁺][OH⁻] equals Kw in any aqueous solution.
steps.memory_tip: Ionic PRODUCT: the two ion concentrations are multiplied, never added.
steps.margin_note: Write the ionisation equation with the ⇌ arrow before the expression.

steps.label: The value at 25 °C
lines: increases, so the value must always be
steps.why: Kw is an equilibrium constant, and every equilibrium constant depends on temperature. The number 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ is true at 25 °C only, so the temperature is part of the answer.
common_mistakes: Writing the value without the temperature. Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ only at 25 °C.
Writing the unit as mol L⁻¹. Two concentrations are multiplied, so the unit is mol² L⁻².
steps.memory_tip: Fourteen at twenty-five: always write the power −14 together with the temperature 25 °C.
steps.margin_note: The value, the unit and the temperature together earn this mark.

insider_note: The value earns its mark only with the temperature written beside it — 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ is true at 25 °C, not in general.
